We don’t have a time sheet for those enquiries. The arrival and key entries support the guests’ waits—48 minutes for A and 86 for B—but those are not staff working minutes.

The staff-time figure comes from our same-evening reconstruction. We estimated 22 minutes for reception: eight reconstructing the promise and handling the initial complaint, seven checking an alternative and explaining the situation, and seven processing the compensation. Housekeeping estimated eight minutes answering repeated progress enquiries. I estimated eight minutes handling the complaint and five checking the refund.

That’s 43 staff minutes, with each interval counted once. It excludes ordinary cleaning and normal check-in. The messages and financial entries support that parts of the work happened; they don’t establish how long each task took. Even the seven minutes for processing the compensation remains an estimate, despite having timestamps for the individual entries. I wouldn’t claim we could recover all 43 minutes.

The 60 GEL refund and 30 GEL waiver were enough for me to notice and check. But I don’t have a complete costed list of that week’s other problems, so I can’t honestly rank this as our biggest loss or give you its share of weekly costs.

Operationally, what concerned me was pulling people into repeated explanations while housekeeping was already short. That was a management problem worth addressing, even without pretending the compensation alone proves a large financial problem.
